## What is a function? {.size-sm}

A **reusable block of code** designed to perform a 
**specific task**. It is executed when called, can take inputs 
(arguments), and can return an output (a value).

[]{.vspace-sm}

::: {.width-50}

```{.r}
# Function definition ----
add_two_values <- function(a, b) {
  
  c <- a + b
  return(c)
}


# Function call ----
add_two_values(3, 4)
## [1] 7
```

:::



## Why write functions? {.size-sm}

Automate repetitive tasks and improve code quality

[]{.vspace-sm}

::: {.grid .text-center}

::: {.g-col-4 .box-shadow}
[{{< fa repeat size=xl >}}]{style="color: #0D657D;"}

[**DRY**]{style="color: #0D657D;"}<br>
[Avoid code duplication]{.size-sm}
:::

::: {.g-col-4 .box-shadow}
[{{< fa puzzle-piece size=xl >}}]{style="color: #805A35;"}

[**Modularity**]{style="color: #805A35;"}<br>
[Build reusable components]{.size-sm}
:::

::: {.g-col-4 .box-shadow}
[{{< fa rotate size=xl >}}]{style="color: #38664B;"}

[**Reproducibility**]{style="color: #38664B;"}<br>
[Ensure consistent operations]{.size-sm}

:::

:::

[]{.vspace-sm}

[**Key benefits**]{style="color: #0D657D;"}

- Improved readability
- Easier maintenance
- Fewer copy-and-paste errors
- Increased productivity


## Anatomy of a function {.size-sm}

::: {.width-66}
```{.r}
function_name <- function(arg1, arg2 = default_value) {

  # Body of the function that builds
  # the result `output`

  return(output)
}
```
:::

[]{.vspace-sm}

[**Key components**]{style="color: #0D657D;"}

- **Definition** - A function is defined using the `function()` keyword
- **Name** - A function can have a meaningful and descriptive name
- **Arguments** (inputs) - A function can take zero, one or multiple arguments
- **Body** - The function body contains the instructions that are executed when 
the function is called
- **Return value** (output) - A function returns a value, either explicitly 
using `return()` or implicitly through the last evaluated expression


## Function workflow {.size-sm}

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
1. **Create an R script**[^rfile]
<br>
Create a `.R` file in the [R/]{.bg-important} directory
:::

::: {.g-col-6 style="margin-top: 0.5em;"}
```{.r}
file.create("R/add_two_values.R")
```
:::
:::

[]{.vspace-2xs}

::: {.grid .fragment}

::: {.g-col-6}
2. **Define the function**
<br>
Write the function definition
:::

::: {.g-col-6 style="margin-top: 0.5em;"}
```{.r}
add_two_values <- function(a, b) {
  a + b
}
```
:::
:::

[]{.vspace-2xs}

::: {.grid .fragment}

::: {.g-col-6}
3. **Source the file**
<br>
Load the function definition into R
:::

::: {.g-col-6 style="margin-top: 0.5em;"}
```{.r}
source("R/add_two_values.R")
```
:::
:::

[]{.vspace-2xs}

::: {.grid .fragment}

::: {.g-col-6}
4. **Call the function**
<br>
Use the function in your script
:::

::: {.g-col-6 style="margin-top: 0.5em;"}
```{.r}
add_two_values(1050, 3234)
```
:::
:::

[^rfile]: You can define one function per `.R` file or group multiple functions in a single `.R` file

## Function arguments {.size-sm}

Arguments define the inputs a function can receive.

1. **Required arguments**: must be provided when calling the function.

::: {.width-50}
```{.r}
add_two_values <- function(a, b) {
  a + b
}

add_two_values(5, 10)
```
:::

. . .

2. **Default arguments**: have predefined values and can be omitted.

::: {.width-50}
```{.r}
add_two_values <- function(a, b = 8) {
  a + b
}

add_two_values(5)
```
:::

. . .

3. **Argument matching**: arguments can be passed by position or by name.

::: {.width-50}
```{.r}
add_two_values(10, 5)
add_two_values(b = 5, a = 10)
```
:::

## Documenting a function {.size-sm}

**Why document functions?**

- Explain the **purpose** of a function

- Describe its **arguments** and **return** values

- Provide usage **examples**

- Improve **readability** and maintainability


## roxygen2 {.size-sm}

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
![](images/roxygen2-logo.png){width=50%}
:::

::: {.g-col-6 style="margin-top: 1em;"}
- An R package used to document functions

- Documentation is written directly **above** function definitions

- Syntax: **`#' @field value`**

. . . 

[]{.vspace-2xs}

```{.r}
#' Add two values
#'
#' Adds two numeric values and returns their sum.
#'
#' @param a A numeric value of length 1.
#' @param b A numeric value of length 1.
#'
#' @return A numeric value representing the sum 
#'   of `a` and `b`.
#'
#' @examples
#' add_two_values(2, 3)

add_two_values <- function(a, b) {
  a + b
}
```

:::

:::
